historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun's History of the Berbers (Kitab al-'ibr al-nawadir fi akhbar al-Maghrib) The name Arzanda carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Arzanda is mentioned in the context of the Berber kingdom of Tlemcen, ruled by the Marinid dynasty. Arzanda was the name of a wealthy woman from Tlemcen who became a prominent figure during the Marinid period. She was known for her patronage of poets and scholars, and her salon was a gathering place for intellectuals and artists.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi's The History of Egypt and the Frontier Lands of the Muslim World (Kitab al-Mawā'iz wa'l-I'tibār bi-Dhikr al-Khitat wa-'l-Athar)
historical_references.context: Arzanda is mentioned as a fortress and a major trading center in the eastern desert of Egypt during the Mamluk period. It was situated near the Red Sea and was an important stopover for caravans traveling between Egypt and Yemen. The name 'Arzanda' is believed to have originated from the Arabic word 'arz,' meaning 'treasure,' reflecting the wealth and prosperity of the town.
